subject: BrightGrid: architecture deep-dive — calendar options & fallback plan

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: BrightGrid: architecture deep-dive — draft agenda + times

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for a great discovery yesterday — really appreciate the clarity on BrightGrid's ingestion pipeline and retention constraints. As discussed, we'd like to run a focused technical deep-dive to cover integration patterns, SLOs, and the model routing fallbacks we sketched.

Draft agenda (attached):
- 5m quick introductions and success criteria
- 20m infra review: data flow, retention, network hops
- 20m serving runtime & routing options (latency vs cost tradeoffs)
- 15m deployment pattern recommendations for regulated data
- 10m Q&A + next steps / mutual action items

Proposed times (PST):
- Tue Aug 3 — 10:00–11:00am
- Tue Aug 3 — 2:00–3:00pm
- Wed Aug 4 — 9:00–10:00am

If none of those work, tell me two windows that do and we’ll rearrange. I’ve attached the agenda and a one-page architecture sketch (redwood-arch-diagram.pdf).

Also looping in Marissa (solutions engineer) and Karthik (infra lead) so they can prep the variant examples and network checklist.

Cheers,
Ben

--
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

- Yes, Karthik will demo the routing fallback and a short cost/latency comparison (we’ll show a 2-variant example: full-precision model + int8 quantized variant).

Hi Alex — quick follow-up from our side with the things we’ll demo and the small ask for network prerequisites.

What we’ll demo (short live demo + slides):
- Live routing scenario: request-level routing between standard and quantized model variants, and automated fallback using cache + prefix hits.
- A small benchmark: latency, p95, and cost delta for 1k QPS simulated across 256 token avg length.
- Recommended autoscaling config for your workload shape (burst vs steady).

Network/permissions ask (helps us avoid a lot of back-and-forth during the call):
1) Can your network lead confirm whether outbound TLS to redwood-public-apis.redwood.ai (443) is allowed for the VPC connector?
2) If you use an egress proxy, can you provide the hostname/ip ranges or confirm we can provide a static egress IP?

If you can paste answers directly into the calendar invite or reply here, we’ll mark them as pre-reads and keep the call focused.

Karthik
Infra Lead | Redwood Inference

Ben / Karthik — thanks, all sounds good. Confirming Wed Aug 4, 2026 10:00–11:00am PST (I sent the invite). I also pasted the network answers below and attached a brief network diagram.

Peak concurrent inference QPS (estimate): 350–450 sustained during peak windows.
Typical sequence length: 160–220 tokens for the primary model; some batched offline workloads spike to 512.

Network answers:
1) Outbound TLS to redwood-public-apis.redwood.ai: allowed (egress rule E-56).
2) Egress proxy present — we can whitelist a static outbound IP range for scheduled calls; I attached the diagram and will share the CIDR list in the invite notes.

We appreciate you including the fallback demo — that specifically will help the execs sign off on a pilot. See you at 10.

Cheers,
Alex
